correctness.rationale: The core gamma-subtracted integral representation and shortest-path Taylor coefficient are derived from exact finite-dimensional spectral calculus. Uniform joint remainders yield a simple rescaled zero for each nonedge, with separately justified negativity below and positivity above the scaling window. Compact-time positivity and a uniform spectral-gap tail exclude further zeros; edges and diagonals remain strictly positive. The P4 logarithmic coefficient is exact from spectral projectors. The standalone checker passed 30,176 numerical tests/evaluations on 12 graphs, but these are corroboration only. Critical steps: For graph distance d>=2, exp(-tL)ij=(W^d)ij*t^d/d!+O(t^(d+1)); (L log L)ij=integral exp(-sL)ij/s^2 ds>0. The local analytic expansion of exp(-t L^(1+epsilon))ij/t has leading terms a*t^(d-1)-epsilon*b. Rescaling by epsilon^(1/(d-1)) yields a unique simple crossing; compact-time positivity and uniform spectral tails exclude others. The diameter dominates the maximum.

originality.rationale: The checked primary literature and closest full published finite-graph result do not imply the graph-distance dependent sharp onset and pairwise unique crossing for arbitrary positively weighted connected graphs. Riascos–Mateos and Benzi et al. treat predominantly 0<alpha<1, Daners–Glück–Kennedy give eventual positivity spectral criteria without this singular perturbation law, and the published complete-multipartite formula covers only a diameter-two subclass. The result derives a distinct square-root (and higher-root) onset at distance three and beyond. Search limitations and historical-priority risk remain.
residual_risks: Semantic search and accessible primary-paper checks cannot exclude unindexed perturbation results under different terminology.
The nearest complete multipartite result covers the special diameter-two behavior; only the genuinely broader distance/weighted conclusions are asserted as new.
Not all potentially relevant monographs or paywalled sources were accessible or reviewed in full.

value.rationale: The sharp diameter exponent 1/(D-1) is a motivated stability invariant for almost-Markovian fractional graph heat. It quantifies the competition between graph-local shortest-path transport t^d and global nonlocal order perturbation epsilon*t. It predicts qualitatively different recovery behavior in arbitrary weighted graphs, including the explicit square-root law on P4, and supplies computable leading coefficients without needing general exact eigenvalue formulas. This is more than a routine reparameterization or known table.
